bib.title: Building Cooperative Embodied Agents Modularly with Large Language Models

question: How can LLMs be used to build embodied agents that plan, communicate and cooperate with other agents and humans under decentralized control, partial observation and costly communication?
hypothesis: LLMs' commonsense, reasoning and language generation, inside a cognitive-inspired modular framework, can yield efficient cooperative embodied agents that beat planning-based baselines.
contributions: Formalized a multi-agent embodied cooperation problem with decentralized control, complex partial observation, costly communication and long-horizon multi-objective tasks, instantiated in C-WAH and TDW-MAT.
Presented CoELA, a cognitive-inspired modular framework (Perception, Memory, Communication, Planning, Execution) that uses LLMs for planning and communication.
Ran a user study of human-AI cooperation with LLM agents.

method.summary: CoELA has five modules; an LLM drives the Communication module (message generation) and the Planning module (zero-shot CoT choice from a multiple-choice Action List); perception uses a fine-tuned Mask-RCNN and execution uses A*-based procedures. Evaluated on TDW-MAT and C-WAH with GPT-4, LLAMA-2-13b-chat and a LoRA-fine-tuned CoLLAMA, plus an 8-subject human study.
method.task: decentralized two-agent embodied cooperative rearrangement/transport with natural language communication

datasets.name: TDW-MAT
datasets.size: 24 test episodes (6 scenes from TDW-House x 2 task types, food and stuff)
datasets.split: 4 floorplans x 3 layouts; two floorplans train, two test; horizon 3000 frames
datasets.source: extended from ThreeDWorld Transport Challenge (Gan et al., 2022); 10 target objects and 2 to 5 containers per task

datasets.name: C-WAH
datasets.size: 10 test episodes (2 tasks x 5 activity types)
datasets.split: horizon 250 steps; 3 to 5 subgoals per task
datasets.source: extended from Watch-And-Help (Puig et al., 2021) on VirtualHome-Social; symbolic and visual observation

datasets.name: Mask-RCNN fine-tuning images (TDW)
datasets.source: randomly sampled in TDW training environments, ground-truth masks from the environment

datasets.name: CoLLAMA trajectories
datasets.size: 2k trajectories from 10 TDW-MAT training episodes, 572 manually filtered
datasets.preprocessing: manual filter for effective communication and good reasoning trace

training.objective: CoLLAMA: LoRA fine-tuning of LLAMA-2-13b-chat on filtered CoELA trajectories (objective not spelled out); MAT: MARL (PPO)

other.MAT input: top-down semantic map (12,24), 9 channels, plus agent info; actions explore/nearest target/nearest container/goal, each up to 50 frames

inference.samples: TDW-MAT: 5 runs for RHP, 1 run for CoELA; C-WAH: 5 runs for MHP, 1 run for CoELA (cost)
inference.prompting: zero-shot chain-of-thought ('Answer: Let's think step by step.') over a multiple-choice Action List; no few-shot demonstrations; Communication prompt = Instruction Head, Goal Description, State Description, Action History, Dialogue History, a closing note, and two seed messages
inference.retrieval: memory retrieval by templates; Episodic memory keeps last K actions and D dialogues (values not stated)

metrics.name: Transport Rate (TR)
metrics.definition: fraction of sub-goals satisfied on TDW-MAT

metrics.name: Average Steps L
metrics.definition: steps taken to finish the task on C-WAH

metrics.name: Efficiency Improvement (EI)
metrics.definition: dM/M0, M the main efficiency metric difference when cooperating vs alone, M0 the larger of the two

metrics.name: Likert rating
metrics.definition: human 7-point rating of communication effectiveness, helpfulness, trust

baselines: MAT (multi-agent transformer, oracle map, central observation)
eval.protocol: Human study: 8 subjects, 10 tasks, each task done by at least 2 subjects, 80 trials, four scenarios (MHP, CoELA, CoELA w/o communication, alone); t-test for trust.

prompts.text: Note: The generated message should be accurate, helpful, and brief. Do not generate repetitive messages.

Alice: "Hi, I'll let you know if I find any goal objects, finish any subgoals, and ask for your help when necessary." Bob: "Thanks! I'll let you know if I find any goal objects, finish any subgoals, and ask for your help when necessary."

I'm Alice. I'm in a hurry to finish the housework with my friend Bob together. Given our shared goal, dialogue history, and my progress and previous actions, please help me choose the best available action to achieve the goal as soon as possible. Note that I can hold two objects at a time and there are no costs for holding objects. All objects are denoted as <name> (id), such as <table> (712).

I'm Alice. My friend Bob and I want to transport as many target objects as possible to the bed with the help of containers within 3000 steps. I can hold two things at a time, and they can be objects or containers. I can grasp containers and put objects into them to hold more objects at a time.

limits: CoELA runs are 1 run per setting because of cost, so no variance is reported for CoELA (Table 1, Table 2).
Test sets are small: 24 episodes on TDW-MAT, 10 on C-WAH.
The authors concede limited use of 3D spatial information, no reasoning over low-level actions, and unstable complex reasoning (counting remaining goals).
Communication between AI agents gave no significant gain; the authors attribute this to the cost of communication and LLM limits.
Ablation values (Fig 4a-c) appear only in figures.
MAT baseline given oracle semantic map and central observation, so not a like-for-like comparison.
Models are 2023-era (GPT-4 API Sept 2023 or May 2023, LLAMA-2-13b-chat).
